stem: Why should a visual symptom chart not be used as proof of a nutrient diagnosis?
choices: Visual symptoms are too subjective to contribute useful evidence.
Different nutrition, root-zone, water, pest, disease, and environmental problems can produce overlapping visible symptoms.
Nutrients rarely create visible leaf symptoms, so charts are mostly historical teaching tools.
EC alone identifies whether a symptom is nutritional, making the chart unnecessary.
rationale: Symptom charts can help organize observations, but many different causes can produce similar chlorosis, necrosis, curling, or spotting. A chart therefore supports a differential rather than proving a diagnosis. The technician should combine visible pattern with pH, EC, irrigation, root-zone, environment, and other relevant evidence before a cause is assigned.
